## Better compatibility with WL 14.0–15.0
We significantly improved symbol rendering, added various styling options for new plotting functions, and improved the output forms of new symbols.

## OpenSUSE and others
We added `.rpm` binaries!

### Exception objects
For example, an `Exception` object now shows relevant information:

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`Exception["DataConsistencyError"]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`Exception[(*VB[*) {"DataConsistencyError"}, <|"ExceptionValidated" -> True, "ExceptionAPIVersion" -> "1"|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

Throw and catch exceptions:

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`CatchExceptions[
	  1+ThrowException[Exception["Null"]],
	  All
	]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`Failure[(*VB[*) "Null", <|"ExceptionAPIVersion" -> "1", "ExceptionTagList" -> {"Null"}|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

### Symbolic array, matrix, and vector representations
...fill in gaps

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`ArraySymbol["a", {2,3}]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(ArraySymbol["a",{2,3}])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAoZgESHvk5KWnMIB4vkAjLTC13SU3OL0osyS8KZgKJOAaDZJUSldKYYHp8MotLgkEmGIFJYwCxxQ9A"*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`MatrixSymbol["a", {2,3}]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(MatrixSymbol["a",{2,3}])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAoZgESHvk5KWlMIB4vkAjLTC13SU3OL0osyS8KBgmH+QYzAymlRCUATnQLww=="*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

and symbolic vectors:

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`VectorSymbol["a", 45]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(VectorSymbol["a",45])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAoZgESHvk5KWnMIB4vkAjLTC13SU3OL0osyS8KZgKJBAeDZJUSlcBcE1MApEMMiA=="*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

Symbolic tensors respect `+`, `-`, and other operations, whereas WL would usually treat them as scalars.

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`a + {1,2,3}
	(*VB[*)(VectorSymbol["a",45])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAoZgESHvk5KWnMIB4vkAjLTC13SU3OL0osyS8KZgKJBAeDZJUSlcBcE1MApEMMiA=="*)(*]VB*) + {1,2,3}`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`{1+a,2+a,3+a}`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`{1,2,3}+(*VB[*)(VectorSymbol["a",45])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAoZgESHvk5KWnMIB4vkAjLTC13SU3OL0osyS8KZgKJBAeDZJUSlcBcE1MApEMMiA=="*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

### Non-commutative algebra representations
We added support for non-commutative algebra symbols. For example:

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`alg = CliffordAlgebra[{{x}, {y}, {z}}]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`NonCommutativeAlgebra[(*VB[*) <|"Multiplication" -> NonCommutativeMultiply, "Addition" -> Plus, "Unity" -> 1, "Zero" -> 0, "CommutativeVariables" -> {}, "ScalarVariables" -> Automatic, "Generators" -> {{x, y, z}}, "Relations" -> Automatic, "CommutationRelations" -> Automatic, "Structure" -> {"Clifford", {{x}, {y}, {z}}}, "VariableOrder" -> "Increasing", "WordOrder" -> "Lexicographic"|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`NonCommutativeExpand[(x + 2 y + 3 z) ** (4 x + 5 y + 6 z), alg]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`-6-3 x**y-6 x**z-3 y**z`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

### Incremental objects
A new feature in recent versions of WL is support for incremental functions and objects, similar to JavaScript function generators and the `yield` keyword.

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`obj = IncrementalObject["Identity"][{1, 2}]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`IncrementalObject[(*VB[*) "Identity", {"Source" :> {1, 2}, "Position" :> 1} (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

Return values from the incremental object:

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`NextValue[obj]
	NextValue[obj]
	NextValue[obj]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`1`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`2`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`Failure[(*VB[*) "IncrementalObjectTerminated", <||> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

### Standard colors
WL's new color palette is now available in autocomplete.

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`StandardBlue
	StandardRed `}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(RGBColor[0.4, 0.6, 1])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNiYGAo5gUSYZmp5S6pyflFiSX5RcEsQBHn4PCQNGaQPAeQCHJ3cs7PyS8qmjUTBG7aFxmDwWP7IgYw+GAPAFRyFkk="*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(RGBColor[0.93, 0.27, 0.27])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNiYGAo5gUSYZmp5S6pyflFiSX5RcEsQBHn4PCQNGaQPAeQCHJ3cs7PyS8qOvxVI6b/0Fv7Io+HVSLr3C8iGAB5sRpI"*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

## Improved formatting of PlotLegends and FrameLabels
Due to a Unicode decoding issue, it wasn't previously possible to embed LaTeX in plot-axis labels or legends, or to mix it with regular labels.

For example, suppose you want to place a LaTeX equation as a plot legend:

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`Plot[x x, {x,0,1}, PlotLegends->Placed[{
	  TeXView["x^2"]
	}, {0.2,0.6}]]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(Legended[ToExpression[FrontEndRef["e8652386-8ccc-4fba-a517-7dcf29fb5173"], InputForm], Placed[LineLegend[{Directive[Opacity[1.], RGBColor[0.24, 0.6, 0.8], AbsoluteThickness[2]]}, {TeXView[Offload[URLDecode["x%5E2"]]]}, LegendMarkers -> None, LabelStyle -> {}, LegendLayout -> "Column"], {0.2, 0.6}, Identity]])(*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

Here we used `TeXView` directly with TeX code inside. Sometimes, if the expression is too large, you may set the size and anchor manually to better position your legend item:

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`Plot[x x, {x,0,1}, PlotLegends->Placed[{
	  TeXView["x^2~\\\\text{function}", ImageSize->{150,30}, AlignmentPoint->{Left,Center}]
	}, {0.2,0.6}]]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(Legended[ToExpression[FrontEndRef["c0121a30-70b4-4e2a-b6ae-a865023f7b39"], InputForm], Placed[LineLegend[{Directive[Opacity[1.], RGBColor[0.24, 0.6, 0.8], AbsoluteThickness[2]]}, {TeXView[Offload[URLDecode["x%5E2~%5Ctext%7Bfunction%7D"]], ImageSize -> {150, 30}, AlignmentPoint -> {Left, Center}]}, LegendMarkers -> None, LabelStyle -> {}, LegendLayout -> "Column"], {0.2, 0.6}, Identity]])(*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

Use `Row` to combine LaTeX expressions with normal text labels.

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`Plot[x x, {x,0,1}, PlotLegends->Placed[{
	  Row[{
	    TeXView["x^2"],
	    "function"  
	  }]
	}, {0.2,0.6}]]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(Legended[ToExpression[FrontEndRef["624aae8d-f789-4f65-8128-44fccff58163"], InputForm], Placed[LineLegend[{Directive[Opacity[1.], RGBColor[0.24, 0.6, 0.8], AbsoluteThickness[2]]}, {Row[{TeXView[Offload[URLDecode["x%5E2"]]], "function"}]}, LegendMarkers -> None, LabelStyle -> {}, LegendLayout -> "Column"], {0.2, 0.6}, Identity]])(*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

The same can be done with the `FrameLabel` of your plot; you can put `TeXView`, or, in general, any other expression, alongside normal text:

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`Plot[x x, {x,0,1}, FrameLabel->
	  {None, Row[{
	    TeXView["x^2"],
	    "function"  
	  }, Spacings->1]},
	  Frame->True 
	]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(FrontEndRef["29a39c5a-c0c3-4217-8c1b-80738bc19f00"])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAoZgESHvk5KRCeEJBwK8rPK3HNS3GtSE0uLUlMykkNVgEKG1kmGlsmmybqJhskG+uaGBma61okGybpWhiYG1skJRtaphkYAAB+ohU4"*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

For example, with a graphic:

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`Plot[x x, {x,0,1}, FrameLabel->
	  {None, Row[{
	    Graphics[{StandardRed, Line[{{-1,-1}, {1,1}}]}, ImageSize->10],
	    "function"  
	  }]},
	  Frame->True 
	]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(FrontEndRef["92c965d7-b00e-40e7-b004-ef923bd81869"])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAoZgESHvk5KRCeEJBwK8rPK3HNS3GtSE0uLUlMykkNVgEKWxolW5qZppjrJhkYpOqaGKSCWSa6qWmWRsZJKRaGFmaWAH7tFUw="*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

## Improved `Sound` support
We have a nice piano-roll preview of a given sequence of notes!

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`Sound[{{SoundNote[{"A4", "C4"}]}, SoundNote["E4"], SoundNote["G4"], SoundNote["C5"]}]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(Sound[{{SoundNote[{"A4", "C4"}]}, SoundNote["E4"], SoundNote["G4"], SoundNote["C5"]}])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAoZgESHvk5KRAeK5AIzi/NS0ljgUn6ZBaXIJQieJwwpX75JalpTMgKgkE8RxMw5WyCRTlYxhWnjDtOGWdTAOEWJA0="*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

We improved our synthesizer pipeline; now we have many instruments!

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`Sound[{
	  SoundNote["C5", {0., .4}, "Piano"],
	  SoundNote["D5", {.5, .9}, "Guitar"],
	  SoundNote["E5", {1., 1.4}, "Violin"],
	  SoundNote["F5", {1.5, 1.9}, "Flute"],
	  SoundNote["G5", {2., 2.4}, "Trumpet"],
	  SoundNote["A5", {2.5, 2.9}, "Organ"],
	  SoundNote["B5", {3., 3.4}, "Marimba"],
	  SoundNote["C6", {3.5, 3.9}, "Vibraphone"],
	  SoundNote["C2", {4., 4.4}, "Drums"],
	
	  SoundNote["C5", {4.5, 4.9}, "AMSynth"], (*WLJS only*)
	  SoundNote["D5", {5., 5.4}, "FMSynth"], (*WLJS only*)
	  SoundNote["E5", {5.5, 5.9}, "DuoSynth"], (*WLJS only*)
	  SoundNote["F4", {6., 6.4}, "MembraneSynth"], (*WLJS only*)
	  SoundNote["G5", {6.5, 6.9}, "MetalSynth"] (*WLJS only*)
	}]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(FrontEndRef["7e531460-c334-45bd-b1bd-94c806387878"])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAoZgESHvk5KRCeEJBwK8rPK3HNS3GtSE0uLUlMykkNVgEKm6eaGhuamBnoJhsbm+iamCal6CYZAglLk2QLAzNjC3MgBAB4VxTu"*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

Here is how you can write a basic 808-style beat:

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true" fade="true" >{`With[{step = 60/140/2},
	  Sound @ Join[
	    (*BB[*)(* closed hats *)(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNhYGAo5gcSAUX5ZZkpqSn+BSWZ+XnFaYwgCS4g4Zyfm5uaV+KUXxEMUqxsbm6exgSSBPGCSnNSg9mAjOCSosy8dLBYSFFpKpoKkDkeqYkpEFXBILO1sCgJSczMQVYCAOFrJEU="*)(*]BB*)
	    Table[
	      SoundNote["C6", {t, t + .035}, "MetalSynth"],
	      {t, 0, 15 step, step}
	    ],
	
	    (*BB[*)(* kick *)(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNhYGAo5gcSAUX5ZZkpqSn+BSWZ+XnFaYwgCS4g4Zyfm5uaV+KUXxEMUqxsbm6exgSSBPGCSnNSg9mAjOCSosy8dLBYSFFpKpoKkDkeqYkpEFXBILO1sCgJSczMQVYCAOFrJEU="*)(*]BB*)
	    {
	      SoundNote["C1", {0, .18}, "Drums"],
	      SoundNote["C1", {3 step, 3 step + .18}, "Drums"],
	      SoundNote["C1", {6 step, 6 step + .18}, "Drums"],
	      SoundNote["C1", {11 step, 11 step + .18}, "Drums"],
	      SoundNote["C1", {14 step, 14 step + .18}, "Drums"]
	    },
	
	    (*BB[*)(* snare / clap on beat 3 *)(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNhYGAo5gcSAUX5ZZkpqSn+BSWZ+XnFaYwgCS4g4Zyfm5uaV+KUXxEMUqxsbm6exgSSBPGCSnNSg9mAjOCSosy8dLBYSFFpKpoKkDkeqYkpEFXBILO1sCgJSczMQVYCAOFrJEU="*)(*]BB*)
	    {
	      SoundNote["C2", {4 step, 4 step + .12}, "Drums"],
	      SoundNote["C2", {12 step, 12 step + .12}, "Drums"]
	    },
	
	    (*BB[*)(* sliding-feeling 808 bass line *)(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNhYGAo5gcSAUX5ZZkpqSn+BSWZ+XnFaYwgCS4g4Zyfm5uaV+KUXxEMUqxsbm6exgSSBPGCSnNSg9mAjOCSosy8dLBYSFFpKpoKkDkeqYkpEFXBILO1sCgJSczMQVYCAOFrJEU="*)(*]BB*)
	    {
	      SoundNote["C2", {0, 3 step}, "Marimba"],
	      SoundNote["G1", {3 step, 4 step}, "Marimba"],
	      SoundNote["Bb1", {6 step, 8 step}, "Marimba"],
	      SoundNote["C2", {8 step, 11 step}, "Marimba"],
	      SoundNote["Eb2", {12 step, 16 step}, "Marimba"]
	    }
	  ]
	]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`(*VB[*)(FrontEndRef["58c0d58d-07d4-4170-8757-1d1ae9932fe7"])(*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNkYGAoZgESHvk5KRCeEJBwK8rPK3HNS3GtSE0uLUlMykkNVgEKm1okG6SYWqToGpinmOiaGJob6FqYm5rrGqYYJqZaWhobpaWaAwB4xxUj"*)(*]VB*)`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

## Music Framework
In WL 15, a new framework was added for working with chords, music lines, and scales. You can find all the symbols under `Music*` using `Names[]`.

In particular, we developed nice preview boxes for notes, pitches, chords, and scales. In general, it follows OOP-like patterns while remaining immutable. For example, here is a single *chord*:

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`MusicChord["CMajor7"]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`MusicChord[(*VB[*) <|"Name" -> "Major Seventh", "Root" -> MusicPitch[<|"Key" -> "C", "Accidental" -> 0|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

**Click on it**

It shows you a tiny piano with notes entering the chord. You can extract a bass pitch, which is a `MusicPitch` object.

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`MusicChord[(*VB[*) <|"Name" -> "Major Seventh", "Root" -> MusicPitch[<|"Key" -> "C", "Accidental" -> 0|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)]["Bass"]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`MusicPitch[(*VB[*) <|"Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "C"|> (*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNmYGAolgISTvkVbvlFuQmORUWJeempKcGlubmJRZVA4TRGkBp+IOFWlJ9X4pqXEpZZVFKamAOREEKScK1ITS4tSUzKSQ1WAQonJ1kYGiWlJOumWhgn6ZqYmFvoWpiaJ+smm5iZWFiapqVZJBulMYAMYQESPpnFJcWsINMSc4pTAbwfKnE="*)(*]VB*)]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

Using pitch and duration objects, you can construct a **note**.

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`MusicNote[MusicPitch[(*VB[*) <|"Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "C"|> (*,*)(*"1:eJxTTMoPSmNmYGAolgISTvkVbvlFuQmORUWJeempKcGlubmJRZVA4TRGkBp+IOFWlJ9X4pqXEpZZVFKamAOREEKScK1ITS4tSUzKSQ1WAQonJ1kYGiWlJOumWhgn6ZqYmFvoWpiaJ+smm5iZWFiapqVZJBulMYAMYQESPpnFJcWsINMSc4pTAbwfKnE="*)(*]VB*)], MusicDuration[1/4]]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Output"  >{`MusicNote[(*VB[*) <|"Pitch" -> MusicPitch[<|"Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "C"|>], "Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/4|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

By grouping individual chords or notes, you can construct a `MusicScore`.

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`MusicScore[{
	  MusicChord[(*VB[*) <|"Name" -> "Major Seventh", "Root" -> MusicPitch[<|"Key" -> "C", "Accidental" -> 0|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)],
	  MusicNote[(*VB[*) <|"Pitch" -> MusicPitch[<|"Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "C"|>], "Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/4|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)],
	  MusicChord[(*VB[*) <|"Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/8|>], "Name" -> "Major", "Root" -> MusicPitch[<|"Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "D"|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)],
	  MusicTransform[MusicNote[(*VB[*) <|"Pitch" -> MusicPitch[<|"Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "C"|>], "Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/4|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)], {"Transpose", 7}],
	  MusicChord[(*VB[*) <|"Duration" -> MusicDuration[<|"Duration" -> 1/8|>], "Name" -> "Major", "Root" -> MusicPitch[<|"Accidental" -> 0, "Key" -> "A"|>]|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)],

If you need scales, there is a special symbol for that:

Construct chords by sampling every third pitch in the list:

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`pitches = MusicScale[(*VB[*) <|"Name" -> "Dorian"|> (*,*)(*"1:"*)(*]VB*)]["PitchList"];
	pitches = 
	  Join[pitches, 
	   MusicTransform[{"Transpose", 12}] /@ Rest@pitches];
	
	Table[MusicChord@pitches[[{i, i + 2, i + 4, i + 6}]], {i, 4}]//TableForm`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

## `Manipulate` colors pre-optimization
`Hue`, `RGBColor`, and `Opacity` can now be used inside Animate, Manipulate, or Refresh in 2D graphics without triggering a full reevaluation:

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`Manipulate[
	  Graphics[{Hue[h, l], Disk[]}, ImageSize->Small], 
	  {h,0,1,0.2}, {l,0,1,0.2}, ContinuousAction->True]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

Just-in-Time transpiler (JIT) will take care of optimizing updates of color/opacity attributes on the graphical canvas.

## Better Mini Apps
We improved our mini apps export feature. Now you don't have to use WLX language at all. Even a single input cell can become an app.

Try this in a fresh notebook and then export this single cell as a mini app using <wljs-html encoded="true">{`%3Csmall%20%3EShare%3C%2Fsmall%3E`}</wljs-html> menu

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`Manipulate[x, {x,0,1}]`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

<wljs-html encoded="true">{`%3Cbr%20%2F%3E`}</wljs-html><wljs-html encoded="true">{`%3Chr%20%2F%3E`}</wljs-html><wljs-html encoded="true">{`%3Cbr%20%2F%3E`}</wljs-html>

## Better autocomplete for Greek letters
We improved UX on typing $\alpha$ and other common greek letters used in math. Start with <wljs-html encoded="true">{`%3Ckbd%20%3EESC%3C%2Fkbd%3E`}</wljs-html> key in the input field:

<WLJSWrapper><wljs-editor display="codemirror" type="Input" editable="true"  >{`⣿`}</wljs-editor></WLJSWrapper>

## File downloading
We introduced a new file container `FrontFileDownload`, that allows to pass any binary data from Wolfram Kernel in a form of a file without touching the file system of OS.

For example:

```wolfram

FrontFileDownload["myFile.png"]
```

or construct it from pure `ByteArray`:

```wolfram
f = FrontFileDownload[ByteArray[{1,2,3}], "test.bin"];
```

Then you can initiate a download file dialog by evaluating the result on the frontend:

```wolfram
FrontSubmit[f]
```

This is helpful for cases where WLJS is running on a server (Docker image), since the usual `SystemDialogInput` will not make sense there, and any `Export` function will operate on the server's local file system.

Alternatively it has a __button-like output form allowing to embed files into the notebook__:

```wolfram
f
```

It will create a download button for a file.

## Fixed bugs
- [x] Unicode issues in `PlotLegends` and other elements that rely on the `FrontFetch` function.
- [x] `Graph` objects are not rendered correctly when their size is less than 1 KB.
- [x] Fixed MCP tool `kernel_evaluate` and summarization issues on nested associations
- [x] `Rasterize` and PDF export stop working after a kernel restart.
- [x] `EmitSound` and `Speak` stop working after a while in the same session.
- [x] Custom windows cannot be made smaller in the desktop version.
